samples.summary: CLI OAuth state token is not bound to the browser that obtained it, so the new `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` consent gate is fully bypassable
samples.evidence:
The web flow binds `state` to a browser via a double-submit cookie (`oauth-state.ts`), but the CLI flow does not: `createState()` stores `{mode, port, nonce, challenge}` server-side and returns an opaque token that is accepted on the callback with **no** cookie/browser check (`auth.controller.ts:167` — `consumeState(stateToken)` then straight to `createCode(user.id, state.challenge)`). The `csrf` field that would have provided that binding is generated (`cli-auth.store.ts:47`), returned, and never verified anywhere (grep: only tests reference it).

Attack, fully scriptable with curl and no victim interaction beyond one navigation:
1. Attacker runs, from their own machine: `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<attacker port>&nonce=<attacker nonce>&challenge=<sha256(attacker verifier)>`. The middleware answers with the confirm page; the attacker reads the `Set-Cookie` secret and the `?confirm=` in the Continue href out of *their own* response (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:106-113).
2. Attacker replays the Continue URL with that cookie. `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` sees `__cliConfirmed` and mints a CLI state token; passport 302s to GitHub, and the attacker reads `state=<TOKEN>` (and `client_id`) straight out of the `Location` header.
3. Attacker top-level-navigates the victim to `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=<app>&scope=user:email&state=<TOKEN>`. Because the victim already authorised the app, GitHub auto-redirects to `/auth/github/callback?code=<VICTIM code>&state=<TOKEN>` with no prompt and no confirm page.
4. The callback takes the `else` branch, consumes the attacker's state, and mints an authorization code **for the victim's user id** bound to the **attacker's** PKCE challenge, then redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<attacker port>/callback?code=…&state=<attacker nonce>` (auth.controller.ts:185-195).

The attacker holds the matching verifier, so whatever receives that loopback hit can redeem access **and** refresh JWTs for the victim at `POST /auth/cli/exchange`. This is precisely the threat the middleware's own docblock claims to close ("mint an auth code **for the victim** and post it to a 127.0.0.1 port of the attacker's choosing"), and it reaches it without ever showing the victim a confirmation page — the consent click is obtained by the attacker against their own cookie. Delivery needs something listening on the victim's loopback (local malware or a co-tenant user on a shared host), which is the same premise the middleware documents. Fix: bind the CLI state token to the browser too (e.g. store `sha256(cookie secret)` alongside it — the vestigial `csrf` field — and require the matching cookie on the callback), and/or bind the state to the confirmed request.

samples.summary: CSV quoting omits `;`, leaving the same neutralizer bypass the branch just fixed for `\r` — a value can still start a new field with a live formula
samples.evidence: `neutralizeFormula` only inspects position 0 of a value (csv.ts:33-42), so it is sound only while a value cannot *become* the start of a field. `NEEDS_QUOTING = /[",\n\r\t]/` (csv.ts:54) covers comma, quote, LF, CR and tab but not `;`. A server-supplied cell/title of `ok;=HYPERLINK("http://evil","x")` is therefore written **unquoted**; opened in Excel/LibreOffice on a locale whose list separator is `;` (most of continental Europe — the same importers the file's own comments cite for the CR and trim cases), the record splits at `;` and column B's content begins `=HYPERLINK(...)`, evaluated on open. Identical shape to the `\r` bypass documented in `docs/tasks/active/...-lessons.md` ("a defence that inspects one position depends on every other layer preserving the framing it assumed"). Quoting `;` (and, for symmetry, `|`) closes it at no cost, since a conformant CSV parser strips the quotes on the way back in.

samples.summary: `findOrCreateUser` (which creates a User, Workspace and WorkspaceMember) runs before the OAuth state check, so a refused/CSRF'd callback still performs database writes
samples.evidence: `githubAuthCallback` calls `this.userService.findOrCreateUser(...)` at auth.controller.ts:115, before the `state` presence check at :144 and the double-submit match at :162. `UserService.findOrCreateUser` (user.service.ts:40-67) creates a `User`, a `Workspace` and an owner `WorkspaceMember` when the email is unseen. So every callback that the new state check refuses — including one an attacker replays through a victim's browser, or simply hits with a stale code — has already provisioned rows. Rate-limited to 10/60s per IP, so impact is bounded, but the state check is a precondition and should run before any side effect.

samples.summary: The CLI-confirmation authorization decision reads `req.__cliConfirmed` with a plain truthy check, which resolves through the prototype chain
samples.evidence: `if (req.query?.mode === 'cli' && port !== undefined && req.__cliConfirmed)` (github-auth.guard.ts:72) is the only thing that distinguishes "the user clicked Continue" from "an attacker navigated the victim here". `__cliConfirmed` is an ordinary string-keyed property, so any `Object.prototype` pollution anywhere in the process (a polluted merge, a prototype-pollution gadget in a dependency reachable from any other route) makes the expression truthy for *every* request and silently unwires the consent gate — the exact failure the guard's docblock says it avoids ("without that flag this degrades to an ordinary browser login"). A `Symbol` key, or `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(req, '__cliConfirmed')`, removes the dependency on prototype hygiene. Same applies to `cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:102` which sets it.

samples.summary: The one-time CLI confirm secret travels in a query string, so it lands in access logs, proxy logs and browser history
samples.evidence: `params.set('confirm', secret)` (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:137) puts the secret half of the consent pair into the Continue URL, i.e. `GET /auth/github?...&confirm=<secret>`. The pino access-log serializer logs `req.url` verbatim (`app.module.ts:69`) and only redacts `authorization`, `cookie` and `set-cookie` — so at `LOG_LEVEL=debug` (or on any 4xx, which is logged at `warn`) the confirm secret is written to logs in cleartext, alongside the OAuth `state` and GitHub `code` on the callback URL. Possession of the secret alone is not sufficient (the httpOnly cookie is also required), which is why this is minor rather than major, but the cookie lives five minutes and log/history readers are a realistic second channel. Consider a POST form for the Continue action, or redacting `confirm`/`state`/`code` from the logged URL.

samples.summary: `__Host-` prefix and `Secure` on both new OAuth cookies are gated solely on `NODE_ENV === 'production'`, so an HTTPS deployment that does not set it silently loses the cookie-tossing protection the module documents
samples.evidence: `isSecureCookie()` (oauth-state.ts:116-118) returns `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`, and both `oauthStateCookieName()`/`hostPrefixedCookieName()` and `oauthStateCookieOptions().secure` derive from it (and `cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:54` duplicates the same test). Any real deployment running over HTTPS with `NODE_ENV` unset or set to e.g. `staging` gets `wafflebase_oauth_state` / `wafflebase_cli_confirm` unprefixed and non-`Secure` — exactly the sibling-subdomain cookie-tossing the docblock at oauth-state.ts:22-47 says the prefix exists to block, plus cleartext transmission. The repo `Dockerfile:88` does set `NODE_ENV=production`, so this is a deployment-posture weakness rather than a live bug; keying the decision on the request being HTTPS (or on an explicit `COOKIE_SECURE` config) would make it fail closed.

samples.summary: `sheets import` now converts any `=`-leading CSV text into a live formula, so importing an untrusted CSV injects executable formulas into a shared document
samples.evidence: `toCellPatch` (csv-parse.ts:90-92) routes any value starting with `=` to `{ formula }` instead of `{ value }`, and it is used on the ordinary positional-grid path too (csv-parse.ts:149), not just the exported `ref,value,formula` table. Previously every imported CSV cell landed as literal text. A CSV received from outside the workspace now writes formulas that every other member's client evaluates. I grepped `packages/core/src` for `HYPERLINK|WEBSERVICE|IMPORTDATA|IMPORTXML|IMPORTRANGE|IMAGE` and found none, so there is no obvious network-egress or exfiltration primitive today and impact is currently limited to computation/DoS-shaped abuse — but the trust boundary moved, and it moved on the grid path that the `--raw` round-trip rationale does not require.

samples.summary: The confirm page is rendered and its cookie minted before any guard runs, so it is outside the global throttler; and both new cookies have fixed names, letting a cross-site GET overwrite a victim's in-flight login
samples.evidence: `ThrottlerGuard` is registered as an `APP_GUARD` (`app.module.ts:122-125`), and Nest middleware runs before guards, so `res.status(200).send(renderConfirmPage(...))` at cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:113 answers unthrottled. Separately, both `wafflebase_oauth_state` and `wafflebase_cli_confirm` use one fixed name at `path=/`, so any cross-site `GET /auth/github` (e.g. an `` on an attacker page) overwrites a victim's pending secret and makes their concurrent legitimate login fail its own state check — an availability nuisance the code comments acknowledge for the tab-vs-tab case but do not mitigate.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element is present as described. The CLI branch of the OAuth callback (auth.controller.ts:165-196) consumes the state token via consumeState() and immediately mints an auth code for the authenticated (victim) user bound to the state's stored challenge, then redirects to 127.0.0.1:<port from state> — with no cookie or browser binding, unlike the web branch (auth.controller.ts:148-164) which enforces the double-submit cookie via webOAuthStateMatches. The `csrf` field that could supply that binding is generated (cli-auth.store.ts:47), returned (:58, :79) and never verified in any production path (repo grep: only specs reference it). The consent gate is self-serviceable: cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:106-113 mints the secret into both the Set-Cookie and the Continue href of the requester's OWN response, so an attacker walks themselves through it; github-auth.guard.ts:72-79 then mints a CLI state token that passport forwards to GitHub (github.strategy.ts:61-68), readable from the attacker's own 302 Location header. The middleware only guards GET /auth/github (auth.module.ts:45-49); the callback is protected solely by AuthGuard('github') (auth.controller.ts:107), so the state is freely transplantable into a victim's GitHub authorize navigation, yielding a code for the victim's user id bound to the attacker's verifier, redeemable at POST /auth/cli/exchange (auth.controller.ts:226-238) for access and refresh JWTs. The nonce cannot help (attacker-chosen) and the port/challenge checks (lines 170-184) do not bind identity. The loopback-listener precondition is the same premise the middleware's own docblock adopts, so it does not refute the finding — it means the added gate reads as covering a threat it does not close. In-lane (auth/CSRF gate bypass, session minting for another principal); critical by impact.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: `NEEDS_QUOTING = /[",\n\r\t]/` (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:54) omits `;`, while `neutralizeFormula` (csv.ts:33-42) inspects only position 0 of a value — a dependency the file's own comment (csv.ts:44-53) acknowledges. No guard elsewhere covers `;`: grep found no other escaping/rejection layer, and the reachable writers (sheets-export.ts:63 writing a .csv a user opens in a spreadsheet, formatter.ts:61) pass server-supplied, cross-tenant-settable values straight through. A comma/quote-free payload such as `ok;=cmd|'/C calc'!A0` matches nothing in NEEDS_QUOTING and is emitted bare; an importer whose list separator is `;` splits the record there and the next field begins with `=`, i.e. the identical framing bypass the branch just fixed for `\r` (tested at test/output.test.ts:155-160, with no `;` case anywhere in the suite). One detail of the reviewer's evidence is wrong — their literal example `ok;=HYPERLINK("http://evil","x")` IS already quoted because it contains `,` and `"` — and the proposed fix is only partly sufficient (quoting shields a leading field but not a later one under a `;`-separator parse). Neither defeats the finding: the missing-`;` gap is real, reachable, unguarded, and formula/CSV injection from untrusted input is in the injection lane, so no named refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope / counterexample) applies.

searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts exchange call (no nonce in body)
finding.summary: CLI auth code is a pure bearer credential — `POST /auth/cli/exchange` requires no proof of possession, even though the new per-attempt nonce is already stored server-side and could bind it
finding.evidence: `createCode(user.id)` (auth.controller.ts:173) mints a code bound to nothing but the user id, and `cliExchange` (auth.controller.ts:203-216) trades that code for full access+refresh JWTs with no authentication and no binding to the login attempt. The code is delivered to the browser as a plaintext HTTP GET: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/callback?code=...` (auth.controller.ts:182), where `port` came off the query string. Anyone who observes that URL — a local listener on the chosen port, a URL-logging local service, a browser extension reading the navigation, browser history/sync — can replay the code within its 60s TTL and obtain the victim's full session. The change already carries the material for a PKCE-style fix: `CliAuthStore` now stores `nonce` per state (cli-auth.store.ts:13), so `cli/exchange` could require the nonce (or a hash of it) alongside the code and reject a code presented without it. It does not. Note this is exactly the direction the confirmation gate cannot cover: once the user clicks Continue on `?mode=cli&port=<attacker's>`, the code goes to a port the attacker picked.

verdict.reason: The claim that POST /auth/cli/exchange has no proof of possession is false in this repository: a complete PKCE S256 binding exists. cliExchange calls consumeCode(body.code, body.verifier) (auth.controller.ts:227) with `verifier` a required, regex-validated DTO field (auth.dto.ts:14-18), so a code-only body is rejected. createCode(userId, challenge) binds the code to the login attempt's challenge (cli-auth.store.ts:101-110) — the reviewer's quoted single-arg `createCode(user.id)` does not exist — and consumeCode verifies sha256(verifier) against the stored challenge with a constant-time compare while burning the entry on every attempt (cli-auth.store.ts:118-128). The callback refuses any CLI login lacking a challenge rather than issuing a weaker credential (auth.controller.ts:179-185), and the challenge is captured at login start in github-auth.guard.ts:73-77. The CLI generates the pair and posts {code, verifier} (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:45-46, 73). Hence observing the plaintext loopback code URL is insufficient to redeem it; the reviewer's proposed fix is implemented under the name challenge/verifier rather than nonce, which is why their nonce-focused greps missed it.
